Resolves #19775

🌿 *A committed drop can no longer leave its proxy behind just because the window it came from let go first.*

When a native titlebar return's source window retires while the owner commit is still pending, the coordinator's release makes the target leave. The leave path's restore is refused, because the pane is already adopted. The settle then skipped its promote because the payload had been cleared. So the proxy stayed live as an invisible empty shell in main. With this change the leave path remembers a payload whose restore the embodiment refused. A late committed completion promotes only that payload's generation, and only while no successor hovers the target. The embodiment identity names item and windows but no generation, so without that fence a late promote would also match a successor that took a restored predecessor's place (RA-1). A departed payload still reports no commit to the coordinator.

Evidence: L3 (headed scene 2 runs on the operator's display, stacked on #19776) → L3 required (AC 3). The AC 2 unit arm is red-first and runs in CI. Residual: none.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — a bounded drop-settlement repair in the two files prescribed by #19775. The original leak is supported by the headed receipt; the new branch also changes completion after a successful restore.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** At `93282cd8960781ce6bb9144e6f9a0d7307ff9454`, a stale committed completion can retire a **successor** proxy. The added condition permits promotion after the payload has changed. [Participation's identity](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/93282cd8960781ce6bb9144e6f9a0d7307ff9454/src/dashboard/dock/window/Participation.mjs#L347-L349) contains only item/source-window/target-window, and [`resolveRecord`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/93282cd8960781ce6bb9144e6f9a0d7307ff9454/src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselProxyEmbodiment.mjs#L353-L364) matches those fields against the currently active record. Neither carries the generation captured by the pending drop.

I ran a deterministic Node probe loading the complete source graph from each Git object, with the standard unit setup, real DragTarget, real Participation stage/restore/promote callbacks, and real VesselProxyEmbodiment. The header-proxy fixture uses real Component instances and stubs only renderer initialization, following the existing embodiment spec.

1. Open header proxy generation 1 for `pane-a`, source window S and target window T.
2. Start `onRemoteDrop` with its owner commit promise held.
3. Call `onRemoteDragLeave`; the actual restore succeeds and retires generation 1.
4. Re-enter with a **new payload**, the same item/S/T, and await generation 2's renderer settlement.
5. Resolve generation 1's pending commit with `{applied:true}`.

| Source | Generation 2 remains active | Generation 2 proxy destroyed | New payload remains current |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parent `298ef00ff2aa63d84a17acbaac9b8c514160f4f8` | true | false | true |
| PR `93282cd896` | false | true | true |

Both return `null` to the coordinator. That return fence is preserved, but it does not prevent the wrong embodiment from being retired. This is a module-composition falsifier, not a claimed headed user-gesture reproduction.

Current-head CI is green: **50 passed, one skipped automerge**. The added unit arm replaces promotion/restoration with array pushes, so it cannot test the generation identity relied on by this change. The headed scene-2 receipt covers the original refused-restore leak, not this restored-predecessor/successor case. `#19776` remains open, as the PR's post-merge replay notes acknowledge.

**Findings:**

- [ ] **RA-1 [P1] — Fence late promotion to the embodiment owned by that pending drop.** At [DragTarget:440–441](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/93282cd8960781ce6bb9144e6f9a0d7307ff9454/src/dashboard/dock/window/DragTarget.mjs#L440-L441), item/window equality is insufficient once the original generation has been restored and a successor uses the same tuple. Preserve the intended cleanup when the original generation's restore was refused, but do not promote or destroy a successor. Add the composed same-item/same-window successor regression using the real embodiment identity path, alongside the refused-restore positive and refused-completion/destroyed-target controls. Correct the claim that an identity-guarded promote necessarily no-ops after restoration.
